subject: Request: Narrow p95 / uptime carveout for SonicWave enterprise deal
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@sonicwave.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@sonicwave.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: SonicWave deal — latency / uptime asks for enterprise pilot

Irene — thanks again for the demo last week. SonicWave is ready to move to a pilot but our security and infra teams flagged a concern: for the pilot to be acceptable internally, we need a written commitment for 99.95% monthly uptime and a p95 inference latency commitment of 120ms for our production traffic (burst-aware).

I understand this is tighter than your standard tier; the customer is paying for a one-year committed capacity plan and procurement has pushed for operational guarantees. Can Redwood provide a carveout or an authorized exception path? If so, we need the asked terms documented in the MSA and a short ops runbook that describes failover/rollback behavior.

Happy to jump on a call this week.

— Alex
Alex Kim
Head of Platform Engineering, SonicWave AI
[attachment: sonicwave_requirements.pdf (PDF)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: SonicWave deal — latency / uptime asks for enterprise pilot

Looping you all in — SonicWave (potential mid-seven-figure ARR) wants a bespoke commitment: 99.95% monthly uptime + p95 <= 120ms. Product and infra implications below.

Top questions for approvals/inputs:
- Marcus: is there precedent to authorize 99.95% for a hosted Dedicated pool with their committed capacity? What SLA carveouts (maintenance windows, force majeure) should we require?
- Marissa: ops/console impact — can we provide an ops runbook + 30-day maintenance blackout for pilot? Also need to estimate the cost uplift for a guaranteed 120ms p95 for their workload profile.
- Connor: legal/procurement will need a short MSA clause and suggested penalty/credit structure. Any redline guidance?

I have a short call scheduled with SonicWave on Wed to confirm non-negotiables. Want to bring an internal position. I attached the requirement summary from Alex.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
[attachment: sonicwave_requirements.pdf (PDF)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: SonicWave deal — latency / uptime asks for enterprise pilot

Quick ops breakdown after an initial perf pass on their sample traces (shared offline):
- To meet p95 120ms consistently we need either (A) dedicated reserved instances pinned to their pool with aggressive KV prefix caching + optimized kernels for gpt-like models, or (B) a quantized model variant with strict batching limits. Option A increases monthly unit cost ~35% vs standard Dedicated; Option B saves cost but may need quality guardrails.
- 99.95% monthly uptime is achievable on Dedicated if we: (1) exclude emergency maintenance windows, (2) configure multi-AZ routing fallback and (3) commit to a 15-minute incident response SLA for P1s during pilot.

Suggested internal ask list to approve before I commit to SonicWave:
1) Pricing uplift approval range: +25–40% (Marcus to set final)
2) Ops blackout: 30 days during pilot start window (agreed to by customer)
3) Fallback policy: allow automated model-variant fallback with notification (customer to accept degraded latency/quality in logging clause)
4) Draft MSA clause & credit cap (Connor)

I attached a draft uptime matrix and an estimate. Happy to review on your Wed sync.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
[attachment: uptime_matrix_v1.xlsx (Spreadsheet)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2026 16:08:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: SonicWave deal — latency / uptime asks for enterprise pilot

Irene — after reviewing the ops notes and the deal economics in HubSpot, we can authorize a conditional exception for SonicWave under these terms: 
- Commitment: 99.95% monthly uptime; p95 inference latency target 120ms for defined workload (pilot traffic shape attached).
- Preconditions: customer signs the Dedicated reserved-capacity contract (12-month), agrees to the 30-day pilot blackout, and accepts the automated fallback policy with explicit degradation logging.
- Financials: pricing uplift set at +30% on top of Redwood Dedicated list for the committed capacity band. Any additional capacity during bursts billed at standard overage rates.
- Credits & limits: standard SLA credit schedule applies up to a 15% cap of monthly fees; force majeure and scheduled maintenance (48h notice) excluded.

Connor — please prepare a redline of the MSA with the above carveouts and a short ops exhibit that describes incident response and rollback. IR: Marissa, please finalize the uptime matrix and send me an ops-runbook summary. I’ll provide executive sign-off once the redline and runbook are ready.

Approved by: Marcus Lin, VP Product & Partnerships
[attachment: sonicwave_msa_redline.pdf (PDF)]
